events.ai_basis: produced a correct argument for the solved problem

why: The only post-snapshot mathematics on the statement itself is Letzter-Pokrovskiy-Williams, an asymptotic gracesize bound: bound, unreviewed, credible. Full-proof claims all predate the snapshot: Mehendale's 2005 claim keeps its 2005 date since the March 2024 v16 shows no identified new mathematics (F1), and it is set aside as not_credible given two decades of silence, math.GM, endless revisions and later work calling the problem open; Gilbert is withdrawn; Gnang 2018/2022 are kept as doubtful (established author, serious method, but a self-acknowledged incomplete lemma proof and no uptake) and are whole/unreviewed, so they tier only as pre-snapshot claims. The Gnang talk restates without new written argument (none). Rideout's posts re-prove known families (none); GPT-5.5 only taught literature, so none. Finite verifications are instances. Kulkarni et al. concerns line graphs, a variant; its ChatGPT 5.1 proof is recorded as generated for that event only, and the variant scope discards it. Adamaszek et al. proves a relaxed labelling, treated as variant rather than bound.
doubts: Mehendale v16 (Mar 2024, 'fully revised', 306 KB to 18 KB) was not read; if it contained a genuinely new argument it would be a post-snapshot claim, though it would still be not_credible on the same signals. Adamaszek et al. could arguably be a bound on an approximate quantity rather than a variant; it is pre-snapshot either way. The Kulkarni verification rests on one unnamed faculty expert, and Clark et al.'s 'digested' rests on journal publication reported by snippet.
